title: Calculator Deluxe
story: The basic calculator from L7 gets an upgrade: floating-point precision, memory operations (MS/MR/MC/M+), calculation history (last 5 operations), clear functionality, and a polished menu. This is a calculator you could actually use daily.
why: Calculator Deluxe demonstrates state management with structs, history with Vec, memory system, and match for operation dispatch — a production-quality utility.
analogy: A scientific calculator with a paper tape printer. The display shows the current number (what you're working on), memory stores a number for later (like a sticky note), and the tape prints every operation (audit trail). Clear resets the display; Clear All wipes everything including memory.
try_it: Add percentage operations (15% of 200 = 30). Add sign flip (+/-). Add undo (reverse last operation using history). Implement a basic expression evaluator that handles '2 + 3 * 4' with correct operator precedence.
tips: Match on Op enum for clean, exhaustive dispatch — compiler warns on missing arms
Cap history at last N entries to prevent unbounded memory growth
Memory is just a second register — store, recall, add-to, clear
common_mistakes: Not checking for division by zero — the most common calculator bug
History growing forever — cap it and remove oldest entries
Integer-only arithmetic when Float64 is needed for fractions and precision
